headline: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told AI companies to own the risks of their technology themselves and dismissed warnings without solutions as poor leadership.
score_reason: A senior cabinet member states the administration's position on AI regulation and China in the same week as the White House accord; read via a relay outlet.
importance_line: The US government is telling the public that AI safety is the companies' job, not Washington's, which leaves people relying on the labs' own promises while the race with China sets the pace; these are one official's remarks in an interview, not a policy document.
summary: Axios reports, as relayed by Bloomberg and The Next Web, that Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said in an interview published on 3 Oct 2026 that "alarmism without solutions" from parts of the AI community "is not leadership" and that "the people at the labs" must accept responsibility for the risks; asked about executives who want regulation, he said "then they should slow down". Bessent also said the US "cannot lose our lead to the Chinese", and the remarks come after Anthropic, OpenAI and xAI chiefs called in September for slowing work on the most advanced models.
notes: Bloomberg original blocked; text read at The Next Web, which credits Axios (interview) and Bloomberg. Axios link not available, so the url is the TNW page.
